title: Private installer: add precheck runner framework + initial checks (k8s version, disk, permissions)
author: Devon Price
description: Context: Private upgrades need a deterministic safety gate before we touch any cluster state. This PR introduces a precheck runner framework inside redwood-private-installer and wires up the first set of checks (k8s version, disk space, and RBAC/permissions). The goal is to standardize how checks are executed, reported (human + machine), and how remediation guidance is surfaced to operators and Support. Summary of changes: (1) New precheck subsystem with a stable result schema (id, title, severity, status, details, remediation, links) and a runner that supports timeouts + parallelism. (2) CLI: `redwood-private-installer precheck run` with default table output and `--json` for support ingestion; non-zero exit code if any BLOCKER fails. (3) Initial checks: Kubernetes version compatibility check against the supported private matrix (min version enforced, plus a warning for versions approaching end-of-support), disk space check for common mountpoints used by the runtime/images, and a permissions check that validates required verbs for installer operations (create/update/list/watch for key resources, plus ability to create Jobs/Secrets in the target namespace). (4) Logging: structured logs for start/end of each check with elapsed time; precheck run emits a correlation id that will be used by later upgrade telemetry work. (5) Documentation: add operator-facing help text for common failures (kubecontext pointing at wrong cluster, insufficient RBAC in namespace, low ephemeral storage). CLI usage: `redwood-private-installer precheck run --namespace redwood-private` Example output (human): `ID  SEVERITY  STATUS   TITLE` / `k8s.version  BLOCKER  FAIL  Kubernetes version supported` / `disk.space   WARNING  PASS  Node disk free space` / `rbac.core    BLOCKER  FAIL  Installer RBAC permissions` Example output (json): includes `results[]` with remediation strings and `exit_code` semantics (BLOCKER failures -> exit 2, internal error -> exit 3). Notes / follow-ups: this is intentionally the framework + first checks only. Storage class detection, snapshot permission checks, and config drift detection are tracked in ENG-2317/ENG-2319/ENG-2320 and will build on this result format. Also note: permissions check currently uses `kubectl auth can-i` when available; when running in fully offline environments without kubectl on the host, we fall back to hitting the apiserver via client-go SelfSubjectAccessReview.
commits: installer/prechecks: introduce Check interface + Result schema + Runner
cli: add `precheck run` command with table output + --json
prechecks: add Kubernetes version compatibility check
prechecks: add disk free space check (nodes + selected paths)
prechecks: add RBAC permissions check (SSAR + can-i fallback)
docs: add precheck usage + remediation examples
tests: unit tests for runner, json encoding, and check behaviors
review_conversation: Sean Gallagher: Disk check: can we avoid false positives on nodes that don’t host the runtime pods? Suggest checking allocatable ephemeral-storage and optionally validating the namespace quota too.

Devon Price: Good call. Updated disk check to report both node allocatable ephemeral-storage (from node status) and free space for a small set of paths when the daemonset can schedule; also added a NOTE in remediation about namespace quotas (tracked as follow-up).
Marcus Lin: For RBAC check, please ensure we don’t log tokens / full kubeconfig contents. Also remediation should point to the least-privilege ClusterRole/Role we ship.

Devon Price: Confirmed: no secrets/kubeconfig content is logged; only api-server host + context name. Added remediation link to the installer RBAC manifest and made the permissions list explicit in the details block.
Ethan Park: Severity semantics: I want BLOCKER/WARNING/INFO to be stable and used consistently later by upgrade orchestration. Also define exit codes now to avoid breaking scripts later.
Devon Price: Added enum docs in `result.go` and CLI help; exit codes are now: 0 (all pass), 2 (BLOCKER failures), 1 (warnings only, with `--strict-warnings` planned), 3 (internal runner error).
Kenji Nakamura: UX: table output is good but the remediation paragraph is hard to scan. Can we add a short remediation summary line and keep the full text in `--verbose`?
Devon Price: Implemented: default output includes a one-line remediation hint; `--verbose` prints full remediation + links + raw details.
merge_summary: Merged via squash after addressing review feedback on RBAC logging hygiene, stable severity/exit semantics, and improved operator output formatting.
release_notes: Private installer now supports `precheck run` to validate cluster readiness prior to upgrades (k8s version, disk capacity, required RBAC).
